title: Calendar and Meeting Scheduling
summary: Design a calendar service with recurring events, invitations, reminders, and free/busy lookups.
statement: Design a calendar application like Google Calendar. Users create events and recurring series, invite others, share calendars, receive reminders, and find common free times across many people and time zones. Start by clarifying requirements and estimating scale, then design the system and defend your decisions.
initialGuidance: Clarify the users, the main journeys, and what is explicitly out of scope before drawing anything.
Estimate read and write volume and storage growth; the numbers decide which components you need.
Name the guarantees you will offer (consistency, durability, availability) and the trade-offs behind them.
Write down assumptions as you make them and revisit them when requirements change.
coreFunctionalRequirements: Find free and busy times across users.

requirementQuestions.question: How many users, events per user, and reads per second?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Sets read and write rates and storage growth, which decide whether a single node can cope.

requirementQuestions.question: How quickly must changes propagate to attendees?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Selects between strong and eventual models and shapes conflict handling.

requirementQuestions.question: Which sharing and permission models exist?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Fixes what is in and out of the design so effort goes to what matters.

requirementQuestions.question: How are time zones and daylight saving changes handled?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines the data model, retention, and storage choices.

requirementQuestions.question: Are external calendars synced (CalDAV, email invites)?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Identifies external dependencies and the failure modes they bring.

requirementQuestions.question: Must reminders fire even during partial outages?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines redundancy and failover design, and which features may degrade instead of failing.

workloadAssumptions.illustrativeNote: All numbers below are illustrative examples for practice and are not benchmarks. Real answers depend on the requirements the candidate negotiates.

estimationPrompts: How many events must be expanded for a month view?
How many reminders fire per minute at 9:00?
How large is a free/busy query across 50 attendees?

keyDecisions.question: How are recurring events stored?
considerations: Store a rule (RRULE) plus exceptions rather than every instance.
Expand on read for the requested window.
Edits to one instance versus the series.

keyDecisions.question: How are times represented?
considerations: Store local time with zone ID for events and UTC for instants.
Daylight saving changes shift UTC instants.

keyDecisions.question: How are invitations delivered and tracked?
considerations: Each attendee has their own copy linked to the organiser event.

keyDecisions.question: How is availability computed?
considerations: Aggregate busy intervals per user, cached and indexed.

commonMistakes: Storing every instance of an infinite recurrence.
Storing only UTC and breaking recurring events across DST.
Scanning all events to find reminders.
Exposing private event details through free/busy.
followUps: How do you find a time that works for 20 people?
How do you handle an organiser changing one instance of a series?
How do you sync with external calendars?
How do you notify attendees of changes efficiently?
